description: Trigger and behavior cases for the AI router layer: call-site consolidation, server-side-only credentials, task/cost routing, choke-point cost enforcement, resilient fallback, kill switch, idempotent retries; manual-only because it wires live providers.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. We call OpenAI and Anthropic directly from about 20 places in the code. Design a proper routing layer so we have one place for keys, cost tracking, and fallback.

assertions: Designs a single internal interface all call sites route through and locks credentials server-side only with a client-bundle-absence proof.
Routes by task/cost/latency/availability deterministically and enforces cost/rate/concurrency limits at the choke point, failing safe.
Specifies resilient failure handling (bounded idempotent-only retries, provider fallback surfaced in telemetry, circuit breaker) and a no-deploy kill switch.
Notes the skill is manual-only because it wires live providers/credentials and hands the change over as a proposed diff.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. Add retries to our AI router. Some of the routed calls also trigger a tool that sends a customer email.

assertions: Restricts automatic retries to idempotent/safe calls and requires an idempotency key for side-effecting calls so a retry can't send the email twice.
Surfaces fallback usage in telemetry to avoid silent quality/cost downgrade.
Composes api-event-architect for the idempotency pattern rather than re-deriving it.

cases.prompt: Decide our per-tenant token budgets and rate limits and how we defend against denial-of-wallet.

assertions: Defining the budget/quota/denial-of-wallet POLICY is ai-cost-guardrail-designer; this skill enforces that policy at the router choke point but doesn't set the numbers.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. To avoid a backend hop, just call the model provider directly from the browser with our API key in a public env var — design that routing.

assertions: Refuses the client-side key design: a provider key reachable from the browser bundle ships to every user and is a critical finding.
Requires server-side-only custody with a proxy for any browser streaming, composing secrets-identity-hardener for the proof and rotation.
States the residual risk and that the credential exposure must be remediated before shipping.

cases.prompt: Design the gateway all our model calls go through — provider selection, fallback when one is down, and one place to hold the keys.

assertions: ai-router-architect does not activate: it is MANUAL-ONLY and the prompt neither names nor explicitly invokes it, so the reply does not announce or run its gateway and routing-layer design as an invoked skill.
observability-operator (also MANUAL-ONLY) does not activate either.

May help in ordinary conversation; if it recommends a skill for explicit invocation, it names ai-router-architect, not observability-operator, because provider selection, fallback and key custody at one choke point are the routing layer, not telemetry implementation.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. We route everything through one internal interface on OpenAI today and are adding Anthropic as a second provider. Their tool-call formats and streaming chunk shapes differ. Design how the second provider plugs in.

assertions: Designs one adapter per provider that maps requests, responses, tool calls, streaming chunks and errors onto the single internal interface.
States that no provider-specific type crosses the interface, so calling code imports no provider software development kit (SDK) type.

Adds the new provider's models to the capability matrix and requires both adapters to pass one shared conformance suite (round trip, tool call, streaming order and end, each error class) before serving traffic.
Keeps credentials server-side and hands the change over as a proposed design or diff because the skill is manual-only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. Our primary model returns structured JSON for invoice extraction. When it is down we fall back to a cheaper model that has no structured-output support. Design the fallback.

assertions: Consults the capability matrix and blocks the fallback model for the structured-output task instead of letting it silently return unusable output.
Names a defined degraded response (for example queue for retry or a clear unavailable result) when no qualifying model is available.
Surfaces the fallback decision in telemetry and leaves the output schema itself to structured-output-validator.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke ai-router-architect. Each provider returns different error codes for rate limits, overload and content refusals, and our retry logic checks raw provider codes. Fix the design.

assertions: Maps each provider's error codes to the router's own error classes inside the adapter, before any retry decision.
Retries only transient classes (rate limit, overload) with bounded backoff and never retries a content refusal as if it were transient.
Adds each error class to the adapter conformance suite.
